title: First Letter Capitalization II
statement:
One table holds pieces of text written by users:

- `user_content(content_id, content_text)`: one row per text; `content_id` is unique. `content_text` contains only English letters, spaces and the characters `\`, `@`, `-`, `/`, `^` and `,`.

A *word* is a maximal non-empty run of characters without a space. Rewrite every word by the first rule that applies:

1. The word begins with something other than an English letter: keep it exactly as it is.
2. The word is two or more non-empty runs of English letters joined by single hyphens (`top-rated`, `FR-ONT-end`): in **each** run, uppercase the first letter and lowercase the rest (`Top-Rated`, `Fr-Ont-End`).
3. Any other word: uppercase its first letter and lowercase every other English letter; other characters stay unchanged (`hello,` becomes `Hello,`, `abc-` becomes `Abc-`).

Spaces, including repeated, leading and trailing ones, stay exactly where they are. Return one row per row of `user_content` with the columns `content_id`, `original_text` (the text as stored) and `converted_text` (the rewritten text). Rows may come in any order.
constraints: content_text is not null and has 1 to 255 characters
content_text contains only English letters, spaces and the characters \ @ - / ^ ,
reference:
WITH RECURSIVE words AS (
  SELECT content_id, content_text, 1 AS word_no,
         SUBSTRING_INDEX(content_text, ' ', 1) AS word
  FROM user_content
  UNION ALL
  SELECT content_id, content_text, word_no + 1,
         SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(content_text, ' ', word_no + 1), ' ', -1)
  FROM words
  WHERE word_no <= CHAR_LENGTH(content_text) - CHAR_LENGTH(REPLACE(content_text, ' ', ''))
),
parts AS (
  SELECT content_id, word_no, word, 1 AS part_no,
         IF(word REGEXP '^[A-Za-z]+(-[A-Za-z]+)+$', SUBSTRING_INDEX(word, '-', 1), word) AS part
  FROM words
  UNION ALL
  SELECT content_id, word_no, word, part_no + 1,
         SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(word, '-', part_no + 1), '-', -1)
  FROM parts
  WHERE word REGEXP '^[A-Za-z]+(-[A-Za-z]+)+$'
    AND part_no <= CHAR_LENGTH(word) - CHAR_LENGTH(REPLACE(word, '-', ''))
),
new_words AS (
  SELECT content_id, word_no,
         GROUP_CONCAT(IF(word REGEXP '^[A-Za-z]', CONCAT(UPPER(LEFT(part, 1)), LOWER(SUBSTRING(part, 2))), part)
                      ORDER BY part_no SEPARATOR '-') AS new_word
  FROM parts
  GROUP BY content_id, word_no
)
SELECT u.content_id,
       u.content_text AS original_text,
       GROUP_CONCAT(w.new_word ORDER BY w.word_no SEPARATOR ' ') AS converted_text
FROM user_content AS u
JOIN new_words AS w
  ON w.content_id = u.content_id
GROUP BY u.content_id, u.content_text;
brute:
WITH RECURSIVE positions AS (
  SELECT 1 AS i
  UNION ALL
  SELECT i + 1 FROM positions WHERE i < 255
),
chars AS (
  SELECT u.content_id, u.content_text, p.i,
         SUBSTRING(u.content_text, p.i, 1) AS c,
         CASE WHEN p.i = 1 THEN ' ' ELSE SUBSTRING(u.content_text, p.i - 1, 1) END AS prev,
         SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING(u.content_text, p.i - CHAR_LENGTH(SUBSTRING_INDEX(LEFT(u.content_text, p.i), ' ', -1)) + 1), ' ', 1) AS word
  FROM user_content AS u
  JOIN positions AS p
    ON p.i <= CHAR_LENGTH(u.content_text)
)
SELECT content_id,
       content_text AS original_text,
       GROUP_CONCAT(
         CASE
           WHEN c = ' ' OR LEFT(word, 1) NOT REGEXP '[A-Za-z]' THEN c
           WHEN prev = ' ' THEN UPPER(c)
           WHEN prev = '-' AND word NOT LIKE '%--%' AND word NOT LIKE '%-'
                AND REPLACE(word, '-', '') NOT REGEXP '[^A-Za-z]' THEN UPPER(c)
           ELSE LOWER(c)
         END
         ORDER BY i SEPARATOR '') AS converted_text
FROM chars
GROUP BY content_id, content_text
notes:
## Intuition

Each word is handled on its own, so first split every text into words on single spaces (two spaces in a row give an empty word, which keeps the spacing intact when the words are joined back). A hyphenated word such as `FRONT-end` needs every part capitalized, so split those words once more, on hyphens. After that, every piece is fixed the same way: uppercase its first character and lowercase the rest, unless its word starts with a non-letter, in which case it is left alone.

## Approach

1. `words` (recursive): word `word_no + 1` is the last piece of the first `word_no + 1` space-separated pieces; a text with k spaces yields k + 1 words.
2. `parts` (recursive): a word matching `^[A-Za-z]+(-[A-Za-z]+)+$` is split into its hyphen parts; every other word stays a single part.
3. `new_words`: capitalize each part when its word starts with a letter (rules 2 and 3), keep it otherwise (rule 1), and join the parts of a word with `-`.
4. The final `SELECT` joins the new words of each text with single spaces in `word_no` order and returns them beside the original text.

## Example 1, step by step

- Text 2, `the QUICK-brown fox`, splits into `the`, `QUICK-brown`, `fox`.
- Only `QUICK-brown` is hyphenated, so `parts` holds `QUICK` and `brown` for it; the other words are one part each.
- `new_words` gives `The`, `Quick-Brown` and `Fox`, so the text becomes `The Quick-Brown Fox`.
- In text 4, `web-based` and `FRONT-end` both split, giving `Web-Based Front-End Development`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(total characters), as each word and part is produced once from its text.
- Space: O(W + P) rows for W words and P parts.

## Pitfalls

- Capitalizing only after spaces turns `top-rated` into `Top-rated`; hyphenated words need every part capitalized.
- Splitting every word on hyphens breaks rule 3: `abc-`, `a--b` and `top-rated,` are not hyphenated words and only their first letter goes up.
- A word led by `@`, `/`, `-` and so on must stay untouched; lowercasing it changes `@USER`.
- Collapsing or trimming spaces changes the text; split on each single space.

## Clauses

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `words` | one row per space-separated word, numbered by `word_no` |
| `parts` | one row per hyphen part of a hyphenated word, or the whole word otherwise, numbered by `part_no` |
| `new_words` | each word rebuilt from its fixed parts as `new_word` |
| `u` | `user_content`, giving `original_text` |
| `w` | `new_words`, joined back into `converted_text` |

narration.1: The recursive CTE words starts with each text's first word: everything before the first space.
narration.7: Each recursive step extracts the next word: keep the first word_no + 1 space-separated pieces and take the last.
narration.9: A text with k spaces has k + 1 words, so the recursion stops after word k + 1.
narration.13: Only words made of letter runs joined by hyphens are split; any other word is kept whole as its single part.
narration.17: Each recursive step extracts the next hyphen part of the word.
narration.19: Splitting continues only for hyphenated words, until every hyphen part has been extracted.
narration.24: A part is capitalized when its word starts with a letter; a word starting with another character is left unchanged.
narration.25: The parts of a word are joined back with hyphens in their original order.
narration.31: The new words of a text are joined with single spaces in their original order, preserving the spacing.
narration.35: One output row per text: group the rebuilt words by the text they came from.
